searchText: https://medium.com/@hongji/eip-1599-is-a-critical-mistake-at-all-433f4416f881 😖 I'm only up to the first argument, but they are arguing against a straw man. 😢 Is this person influential enough to take the time to argue against? There are a number of issues with their third point analysis, but surfacing them will be non-trivial. Hm, yeah, the arguments i've read so far are pretty weak > But EIP-1559 is actually supposed that depriving miners of revenue getting from Gas can make gas cheaper. No one said EIP-1559 would make gas cheaper? At least none of the proponents I know. Seems weird to argue on that point Yeah. It is a strawman. I kind of understand it, because there is a misconception among laymen that it will "fix gas prices" which to many means "lower gas prices". Right Point 2 seems to be a minor misconception that I was arguing that current mining has an incentives problem and 1559 doesn't, when in reality I was just debunking a common argument I saw on the internet. Point 3 is hard to follow, but I believe they have a number of errors in their argument but discussing those problems will be a lengthy and complicated process. They made a similar post ~1.5 years ago that I argued against This gets us to the whole, "should we spend time arguing with every wrong person on the internet" problem? Yeah, the arguments are weak, but they're time-consuming to respond to yes, they wrote a similar piece a few years ago time responding to this would be better spent getting the current client teams onboard (See: Brandolini's law) I mentioned this to someone in a 1:1 call today, but worth sharing here as well: it seems like reducing MEV may be a really strong motivation for 1559 (i.e. if we have huge txn fees that don't get burned, the risk of re-orgs to capture those rises), but I haven't seen a clear, "blog-post-level" explanation of it. If anyone is interested in taking a stab at this, I think it could provide value in the discourse around the EIP. I'm sure <@456226577798135808> and <@!528251935829262351> have some thoughts on this, and others as well 😄 There was a good discussion on MEV and security on the bankless podcast with charlie noyes http://podcast.banklesshq.com/26-eth-has-to-be-money-charlie-noyes (towards the last 30 minutes) One takeaway might be that if bots keep going into bidding wars there may still be substantial MEV despite the burning
